microtheory.name: markov_chains_mixing
microtheory.definition: Markov chains, mixing times, ergodic theory, random walks on graphs, spectral graph theory. Mathematical framework for stochastic processes on state spaces. Grounds Paper 1's Theorem XIII (Substrate-Markov-mixing efficiency, conjecture): substrate's dynamics as random walk; mixing time bounded by spectral gap; efficient substrate has high Cheeger constant + bounded second eigenvalue.

concepts.name: markov_chain
concepts.definition: Stochastic process where next state depends only on current. Markov property: P(X_{n+1}|X_n, ..., X_0) = P(X_{n+1}|X_n). Substrate analogue: substrate's σ-state transitions.

concepts.name: markov_property
concepts.definition: Memorylessness. Future depends only on present, not history. Substrate analogue: substrate's current-state-suffices dynamic.

concepts.name: transition_matrix
concepts.definition: P[i][j] = P(go from i to j in one step). Rows sum to 1 (right-stochastic). Substrate analogue: substrate's σ-update operator.

concepts.name: state_space_mc
concepts.definition: Set of possible states. Finite or countable for classical theory; continuous extensions exist. Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-state space.

concepts.name: stationary_distribution
concepts.definition: π such that πP = π. Long-run state distribution. Substrate analogue: substrate's equilibrium basin distribution.

concepts.name: ergodic_markov_chain
concepts.definition: Irreducible + aperiodic. Converges to unique stationary distribution from any start. Substrate analogue: substrate's well-conditioned dynamics.

concepts.name: irreducibility
concepts.definition: Every state reachable from every other. No isolated components. Substrate analogue: substrate's connected-Mt-space.

concepts.name: aperiodicity
concepts.definition: No fixed period of returns. Avoids oscillation. Substrate analogue: substrate's varied tick patterns.

concepts.name: detailed_balance
concepts.definition: π_i P[i][j] = π_j P[j][i]. Time-reversibility. Common in physics-derived chains. Substrate analogue: substrate's symmetric coupling.

concepts.name: mixing_time
concepts.definition: t_mix(ε) = min{t: max_x ||P^t(x,·) - π||_TV ≤ ε}. Time to approach stationary distribution within ε. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-convergence time.

concepts.name: total_variation_distance
concepts.definition: TV distance between distributions. ||P-Q||_TV = sup_A |P(A) - Q(A)|. Substrate analogue: substrate's distribution discrepancy.

concepts.name: fast_mixing
concepts.definition: t_mix polynomial in log|state_space|. Substrate analogue: substrate's efficient-relaxation.

concepts.name: slow_mixing
concepts.definition: t_mix exponential. Often correlated with phase transitions, bottlenecks. Substrate analogue: substrate's stuck-basin failure mode.

concepts.name: cutoff_phenomenon
concepts.definition: Mixing time has sharp transition. Diaconis. Substrate analogue: substrate's phase-transition dynamics.

concepts.name: spectral_gap
concepts.definition: 1 - |λ_2| where λ_2 is second-largest eigenvalue of transition matrix (in absolute value). Larger gap = faster mixing. THE KEY QUANTITY FOR PAPER 1 THEOREM XIII. Substrate analogue: substrate's mixing-efficiency primary measure.

concepts.name: second_eigenvalue_lambda2
concepts.definition: Second-largest eigenvalue (by |·|) of stochastic matrix. λ_1 = 1 always. λ_2 controls mixing rate. Substrate analogue: substrate's slowest-decay mode.

concepts.name: mixing_eigenvalue_bound
concepts.definition: t_mix(ε) ≤ (1/(1-λ_2)) · log(1/ε π_min). Spectral mixing bound. Substrate analogue: substrate's spectral-controlled mixing.

concepts.name: cheeger_inequality
concepts.definition: Cheeger 1970. Spectral gap bounded by isoperimetric Cheeger constant: φ²/2 ≤ 1-λ_2 ≤ 2φ. Substrate analogue: substrate's geometric bottleneck = spectral bottleneck.

concepts.name: cheeger_constant_conductance
concepts.definition: φ(G) = min_S φ(S). Measures how 'bottlenecked' the chain is. Small φ = bottleneck = slow mixing. Substrate analogue: substrate's geometric mixing barrier.

concepts.name: conductance
concepts.definition: φ(S) = (Σ_{i∈S,j∉S} π_i P[i][j]) / π(S)π(S^c). Edge-cut weighted by stationary probabilities. Substrate analogue: substrate's basin-boundary flux.

concepts.name: random_walk_graph
concepts.definition: Markov chain on graph: from vertex v, go to uniform random neighbor. Substrate analogue: substrate's stochastic traversal.

concepts.name: lazy_random_walk
concepts.definition: Stay put with probability 1/2, else move. Ensures aperiodicity. Substrate analogue: substrate's reflexive σ-update.

concepts.name: expander_graph
concepts.definition: Sparse but well-connected. Cheeger constant bounded below. Fast mixing. Substrate analogue: substrate's small-world Mt-connectivity.

concepts.name: spectral_graph_theory
concepts.definition: Studies graph properties via eigenvalues of associated matrices (adjacency, Laplacian). Substrate analogue: substrate's structural spectrum.

concepts.name: graph_laplacian
concepts.definition: L = D - A. D=degree, A=adjacency. Eigenvalues: 0 = λ_1 < λ_2 ≤ ... Substrate analogue: substrate's Mt-graph Laplacian.

concepts.name: algebraic_connectivity
concepts.definition: λ_2(L). Fiedler value. Larger = better connectivity = faster mixing. Substrate analogue: substrate's connectivity strength.

concepts.name: metropolis_hastings
concepts.definition: MCMC algorithm. Accept/reject based on density ratio. Detailed balance. Substrate analogue: substrate's proposal-acceptance dynamics.

concepts.name: gibbs_sampling
concepts.definition: MCMC. Sample each variable conditional on others. Substrate analogue: substrate's per-Concept update.

concepts.name: coupling_argument
concepts.definition: Bound mixing by coupling two chains: when they meet, both at stationary. Substrate analogue: substrate's parallel-substrate convergence.

concepts.name: ergodicity
concepts.definition: Time averages = ensemble averages. Long-run frequency equals stationary probability. Substrate analogue: substrate's time-average behavior.

concepts.name: ergodic_theorem
concepts.definition: For ergodic chain: lim (1/n) Σ f(X_i) = E_π[f] almost surely. Substrate analogue: substrate's empirical-expectation convergence.

concepts.name: mixing_time_efficiency_paper1
concepts.definition: Paper 1 Theorem XIII conjectures substrate's mixing time scales as a function of Γ quality. Higher-quality Γ → smaller bottleneck → larger spectral gap → faster mixing. Substrate analogue: literally what Paper 1 conjectures.

rules.name: spectral_gap_bounds_mixing_time
rules.head: Jabberwock evaluates Paper 1 Theorem XIII
rules.body: the theorem's central quantity is the spectral gap (1 - λ_2). t_mix ≤ (1/(1-λ_2)) · log(1/ε π_min). Bigger gap = faster mixing. Substrate's efficient mixing requires bounded λ_2.

rules.name: cheeger_links_geometry_to_spectrum
rules.head: Jabberwock analyzes its substrate's mixing
rules.body: geometric bottlenecks (low conductance) imply spectral bottlenecks (small spectral gap). Cheeger inequality. Substrate's structural well-connectedness = mixing efficiency.

rules.name: ergodicity_required_for_convergence
rules.head: Jabberwock's chain reaches stationary distribution
rules.body: the chain must be ergodic (irreducible + aperiodic). Otherwise no convergence. Substrate's dynamics must satisfy this for predictable behavior.

rules.name: expander_graphs_have_efficient_mixing
rules.head: Jabberwock's Mt-graph is well-connected (expander-like)
rules.body: Cheeger constant bounded below; spectral gap bounded above zero; mixing time logarithmic in state-space size. Substrate's efficient-substrate condition.

rules.name: mcmc_provides_sampling_for_complex_distributions
rules.head: Jabberwock needs to sample from complex posterior
rules.body: MCMC (Metropolis-Hastings, Gibbs) provides the machinery. Detailed balance + ergodicity ensure correctness. Substrate's Bayesian sampling.
